page_title: Codewars - Achieve mastery through coding practice and developer mentorship

summary.title: Codewars
summary.one_liner: Codewars is a coding practice site where you solve community-authored small exercises called kata, with in-browser test cases and ranks, in 55+ programming languages.
takeaways: Kata are small coding exercises authored by the community, checked with test cases in the browser.
Kata are ranked from beginner to expert, and completing higher-ranked kata raises your rank and honor.
You can compare your solution with others after completing a kata and discuss techniques.
The site supports over 55 programming languages, so you can practice a new language on familiar problems.
Users can author their own kata to train specific skills.
summary.summary: The Codewars homepage presents the site as a practice platform for small coding exercises called kata, which are written and shared by its user community. It describes solving kata in the browser with test-driven checks, earning ranks and honor as difficulty increases, and comparing solutions with other users after each kata. The page also lists community stats (75K+ new members monthly, 1M+ kata completed monthly, 12K+ kata created) and mentions a separate assessment product for organizations. It contains no detailed technical documentation.
